sections.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) struggle with position bias in multi-image reasoning, where predictions are significantly altered by image placement. This paper introduces Position-wise Question Answering (PQA) to quantify reasoning at specific positions, revealing that open-source models exhibit recency bias while proprietary models like GPT-4o struggle with middle-positioned images. To mitigate this, the authors propose SoFt Attention (SoFA), a training-free method using linear interpolation between causal and bidirectional attention. SoFA reduces position bias and improves reasoning performance by 2-3% on multi-image benchmarks. Code: https://github.com/xytian1008/sofa.
sections.introduction: While LVLMs have advanced to multi-image tasks, their reasoning processes regarding inter-image relationships remain poorly understood. Inspired by the 'lost in the middle' phenomenon in NLP, the authors investigate position bias in LVLMs. Preliminary experiments on benchmarks like BLINK and MuirBench show that shuffling image order causes prediction inconsistency in models like OpenFlamingo and GPT-4o. Related work highlights that while position bias is known in LLMs, its systematic impact on LVLMs is under-explored. This study aims to identify these bias patterns and provide a robust mitigation strategy.
sections.method: The authors introduce Position-wise Question Answering (PQA), a task requiring independent reasoning across images to identify position-specific performance. To address identified biases, they propose SoFt Attention (SoFA). Standard attention is defined as: $Q = \mathcal{P}(XW_q, pos)$, $K = \mathcal{P}(XW_k, pos)$, and $H = \text{Softmax}(QK^T/\sqrt{d}) \odot \mathbb{1}_{causal}V$. SoFA modifies this by interpolating between causal and bidirectional masks: $H_{soft} = \text{Softmax}(QK^T/\sqrt{d}) \odot M_{soft}V$, where $M_{soft} = (1 - \sigma)\mathbb{1}_{causal} + \sigma\mathbb{1}_{bidirectional}$. The parameter $\sigma$ controls bidirectional interaction. To preserve pre-trained alignment, SoFA is applied every two layers.
sections.experiments: SoFA is evaluated using open-source models including Idefics2-8B, InternVL2-8B, VILA-13B, Mantis-8B, and LLaVA-NeXT-Interleave-7B. Testing spans benchmarks such as BLINK, Mantis-Eval, MuirBench, MIRB, NLVR2, and MVBench. The study also utilizes the Multi-modal Haystack benchmark to test long-context capabilities up to 100 images. Ablation studies focus on the interpolation parameter $\sigma$ and the frequency of SoFA layer application.
sections.results: PQA analysis shows open-source models have a strong recency bias, while GPT-4o exhibits a U-shaped curve. SoFA significantly reduces prediction inconsistency (e.g., Idefics2 on BLINK drops from 41.55% to 12.36%) and improves average accuracy by 2-3%. It enhances in-context learning and long-context performance, with gains up to 5.92% at 100 images. Task-specific improvements are highest in visual retrieval (6.84%) and analogy (5.53%). Attention visualization confirms SoFA smooths the distribution across images. Optimal $\sigma$ values vary by task: video tasks require lower $\sigma$ to maintain temporal order, while image-pair tasks benefit from higher $\sigma$.
sections.conclusion: This research identifies and quantifies position bias in multi-image LVLMs, distinguishing between the recency bias of open-source models and the middle-sequence struggles of proprietary models. The proposed SoFt Attention (SoFA) serves as an effective, training-free mitigation strategy. By interpolating causal and bidirectional attention, SoFA enhances the robustness, reliability, and overall reasoning performance of LVLMs across diverse multi-image and long-context scenarios.
